5.0.s.en: (1) Holofernes inquires about the strength of the children of Israel

5.0.0.en: Was enraged: was angry with violent fury.

5.0.2.en: Moab: the descendants of Lot, a people neighboring the children of Israel, dwelling on the eastern bank of the river Jordan, who were at odds with the children of Israel most of the time.

5.0.3.en: The children of Ammon: also descendants of Lot, dwelling beside the children of Israel, east of the Dead Sea and south of Moab. They too were at odds with the children of Israel, like the children of Moab.

5.0.4.en: The news of the preparations of the children of Israel for war reached Holofernes – the commander of the Assyrian armies – through his spies, whom he had sent ahead of him everywhere. He became very angry, because he had not expected anyone to try to fight him, as a result of his extreme pride and his earlier victories, which made him despise all the nations of the world and their gods. But at the same time he was disturbed, and with his military experience he began to gather information about the children of Israel. He found no better source than their neighbors, whose lands he had taken and who had surrendered to him, to ask them about the children of Israel. The most important of these were the peoples of Moab and the children of Ammon, who dwell east of the Jordan, opposite the land of the Jews and the plain of Esdraelon, which lies west of the Jordan (ch. 4:5).

5.1.0.en: They gathered for Holofernes the military leaders of Moab and the children of Ammon, and they stood before him. Holofernes, in extreme anger and rage, asked them, inquiring about the military strength of the children of Israel, and demanded details about their cities and how well fortified they were, the strength of their armies, their numbers, and the commander of their armies. Then he asked in disapproval and astonishment how they had made light of his great army and had not submitted to him like the rest of the lands of the world, but had prepared to fight him!

5.1.1.en: So the devil always makes light of the children of God in their apparent weakness, forgetting the power of God hidden in them, as Goliath made light of David, but was killed by his hands, and as Satan made light of saints such as St. George and St. Anthony, but was defeated by them.

5.1.2.en: Do not take the outward, superficial view, for the small and weak may be mighty because God is with him, and on the contrary the great and mighty may be weak because God has left him. Do not make light of yourself however weak you may be, but prepare to fight the devil and be confident that you are able to triumph over him, however great his power and the power of his wicked helpers.

5.2.s.en: (2) Achior explains the history of the children of Israel

5.2.0.en: Achior: the supreme commander of all the armies of the children of Ammon; the meaning of his name is brother of light.

5.2.1.en: Achior came forward courageously from among the commanders of the armies of Moab and the children of Ammon and stood before Holofernes, and declared with great humility his readiness to tell him all the truth about the children of Israel who dwell in the mountains and about their strength.

5.3.0.en: The Chaldeans: the inhabitants of Chaldea, which lies south of Babylon; they are the original inhabitants of the region of Mesopotamia.

5.3.1.en: Mesopotamia: between the rivers Tigris and Euphrates, which lie in the present country of Iraq. Ways: laws and forms of worship.

5.3.2.en: Achior told Holofernes that the origin of the children of Israel was the Chaldeans, who dwell in Mesopotamia. They are the descendants of Abraham, and they left the pagan gods and all the worship and rites connected with them, and believed in God the Creator of heaven and earth and worshiped Him.

5.4.0.en: The God of heaven: a name of the God of the children of Israel, by which He was known anciently among the nations.

5.4.1.en: Achior recounted the history of the children of Israel briefly, speaking of Abraham and his seed in the plural, that is, that they are the people of God who left their original land according to God's command, then went down to Egypt and multiplied there. Abraham worshiped God while he was in Mesopotamia, in Ur of the Chaldeans, and offered Him worship of prostration and prayers. Then God commanded him to leave his land and go to Canaan. He passed first through Haran in the north of Mesopotamia and dwelt in it until his father Terah died, then went to Canaan and stayed in it until he died, then his son Isaac, and after him his grandson Jacob. When the famine spread over all the world, Jacob and his sons went down to Egypt, and Joseph his son, who was ruler over Egypt, received them as guests, and they multiplied there for about four hundred years, until their number reached about two million, so that they were like a great army because of their numbers.

5.5.0.en: Dealt hardly with them: was severe in his treatment of them and multiplied hardships upon them.

5.5.1.en: Clay and brick: brick is the unbaked block, and clay is what binds the bricks together. Later, building developed, so they came to burn the bricks, which became red brick, and instead of using clay they now use cement.

5.5.2.en: When the number of the children of Israel increased in Egypt, the king feared them and was severe in his treatment of them and made them labor at building cities and humbled them greatly. They cried out to their God, who intervened and struck Egypt by the hand of Moses with the ten plagues, so that Pharaoh of Egypt might submit and allow the children of Israel to go out from him.

5.6.0.en: Their rear: that is, those who were waiting for them from their families in Egypt, whom they left behind them when they went out to pursue the children of Israel.

5.6.2.en: Dry land: what is meant is the land, that is, the solid ground found on the floor of the sea.

5.6.3.en: The tenth plague with which God struck Egypt was the hardest of the plagues, for in it all the firstborn in Egypt were struck, so Pharaoh was compelled in fear to let the people of the children of Israel go. But after their departure he felt that he had lost a great number of workers who had been helping him for nothing, so he went out after them to bring them back to Egypt by force. The children of Israel had reached the Red Sea, and God divided the sea for them, so that the waters became like a wall on both sides, and the children of Israel crossed on the ground at the bottom of the sea. Even so the Egyptians were not afraid, but pursued them. After the children of Israel came out of the sea, Moses struck the sea, and Pharaoh and all the army of the Egyptians were drowned, and not one of them remained to tell those who dwelt in Egypt what had happened to them; rather, the news of this great event spread and reached Egypt.

5.6.4.en: This is the power of God in His children who obey Him: even if He lets them endure many afflictions, He returns and saves them with a great power that no one expects. So be patient, my brother, in affliction, obeying the commandments of God, confident that He will lift from you all your troubles and humble for you all the demons that fight you, so that you are assured of complete victory over them.

5.6.5.en: You must be estranged from the world and leave your family and your kindred like Abraham, then accept affliction in the land of Egypt, and then God appears and makes your enemies afraid. Then you pass through the sea, that is, in Baptism, and die with Christ and rise with Him, and by that you triumph. In every repentance, confession and Communion you experience that victory, and your striving is completed when you pass over this world and rise with Christ on the last day.

5.7.0.en: Then God's care for His children appears in the midst of afflictions and hard circumstances that cannot be borne. In the barren wilderness of Sinai, where an ordinary person cannot live, two million human beings lived under the care of God.

5.8.0.en: In the wilderness of Sinai the children of Israel found no water to drink, so God turned the bitter water into sweet water for them; and they found no food, so He sent down manna for them from heaven. And for forty years God continued to sustain them and give them their food and drink in the wilderness.

5.9.0.en: Shield: a piece of wood usually covered with leather, with a loop behind it into which the soldier puts his hand. This shield is used to protect his head and body from the arrows aimed at him.

5.9.1.en: The people of God in the wilderness of Sinai were exposed to attack by enemies, such as the Amalekites, who were strong men of huge bodies. They triumphed over them easily by the power of God and not by weapons of war, which have no strength against the power of these enemies.

5.9.2.en: Therefore let my heart be at rest, because "The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want": He supplies my needs in the midst of afflictions and fights for me against my enemies the demons, so that I rise from my sins and triumph over them and rejoice at all times.

5.10.0.en: The children of Israel remained strong, and none could overcome them unless they abandoned the worship of God; then their shame and weakness appeared and their enemies triumphed over them. This happened often in the age of the Judges, when the people worshiped the idols of the nations around them and intermarried with them, so these lands rose against them and occupied them and humbled them and plundered their spoil and possessions, as is clear in the Book of Judges.

5.11.0.en: The Canaanites, the Jebusites, the Perizzites, the Hittites, the Hivites and the Amorites: the peoples who dwelt east and west of the river Jordan, whom Joshua triumphed over and whose lands he possessed.

5.11.1.en: Heshbon: a city of Moabite origin, in which King Sihon the Amorite reigned, lying east of the river Jordan between the rivers Arnon and Jabbok. Moses took possession of it and gave it to the tribe of Reuben. If the children of Israel repent of their sins and return to God and worship Him, He gives them power to overcome all their enemies, as happened after their defeat before Ai in the days of Joshua, when they repented and triumphed over the kings of the land of Canaan and occupied their lands, and as David and Solomon triumphed and subdued the peoples around them, as is mentioned in the books of First and Second Samuel and First Kings.

5.11.2.en: They kept their strength and God's dwelling in their midst as long as they held fast to His commandments and His worship and kept far from evil, because their God hates evil.

5.12.0.en: Achior gave an example to confirm his words: when the people of God departed from His worship and worshiped idols, they became weak, so the Assyrians overcame them and took possession of their lands, and even reached their capital Jerusalem – in the days of King Manasseh – and seized him, and of course took many of the leaders and men of war from Jerusalem and carried them to Babylon, and they remained there until Manasseh repented in the prison of Babylon, and God had mercy on him and brought him back, with those of his people who had been taken captive, to Jerusalem and the mountains of Judea, and they possessed them again (2 Chr 33:11-13).

5.12.1.en: I wish, my brother, that you would be confident that it is sin that makes us lose the care and fatherhood of God. So let us hold fast to His commandments and repent of our sins, and He will forgive them for us in the sacraments of confession and Communion, and we will enjoy His protection and His power working in us.

5.13.s.en: (3) The advice of Achior and the anger of Holofernes

5.13.0.en: Yoke: a crosswise piece of wood from the middle of which another piece of wood projects at right angles, to the end of which the agricultural implement is attached; the crosswise piece is placed on the necks of two animals that draw this implement. The yoke is a symbol of domination, and what is meant here is the power of authority and the control and enslavement of the people by Holofernes. We are not able to withstand them: we cannot face them, because they are much stronger than we.

5.13.1.en: Achior gave Holofernes clear and sincere guidance about his plan of war for fighting the children of Israel, drawn from the facts he had recounted about them, which are summarized as follows:

5.13.2.en: 1- No one can resist the power of the God of the children of Israel; rather, he becomes a reproach and a shame before Him.

5.13.3.en: 2- God does not leave His people unless they sin, and then they become weak and can be overcome.

5.13.4.en: 3- Their condition must be learned: if they have fallen into sin and God is angry with them, they are without strength and can be fought and overcome. But if they worship Him faithfully and uprightly, let us keep away from them, because their strength surpasses every power on earth.

5.13.5.en: If others know the power of our God that is in us and bear witness to it, shall we not hold fast to our faith and trust in our God, and not be terrified by the powers of the world?

5.14.0.en: When the commanders of the armies, the assistants of Holofernes, who were standing in his presence, heard the words of Achior, they were very angry, for it was the first time they had heard of a power that could stand before them. They were drowned in pride, thinking they were the strongest power in the world, and they made light of the children of Israel, since their number was small and their military experience weak, and therefore – in their view – their God was weak before Nabuchodonosor, whom they thought to be the strongest god in the world, and they were trying to prove this. So they felt that Achior was loyal to the children of Israel and deceiving Holofernes, and they tried to kill him for his boldness in saying these words, declaring the power of the children of Israel and their God.

5.15.0.en: Given up to the sword: deserving to be killed by the sword.

5.15.1.en: Despite the rage of the men of Holofernes and their desire to kill Achior, they postponed it until they should take possession of the land of the Jews and destroy it and kill those in it, with Achior among them, in order to declare to the whole world that the strongest god in the world is Nabuchodonosor king of the Assyrians.

5.15.2.en: So the pride of man makes him forget the power of God and reject any testimony to Him. I wish that you would not reject the opinions of others that God may send to you to bear witness to Him, or to call you to humility and repentance. Achior is not a deceiver but a witness to God. Look, lest God has sent you an Achior in your wife, or your husband, or your father, or your mother, or your son, or your daughter, or your friend, or any person around you, and you reject his words in pride, that is, the voice of God sent to you. The voice may be very clear and supported with proofs, like the words of Achior, and you reject it as you reject the words of the Holy Bible, the guidance of your father of confession and the teachings of the Church, and then you go further in boldness, rebuking and insulting the one who declares to you the voice of God, even trying to kill him, that is, to silence the voice of God, so that you may remain in your sin.

6.0.s.en: (1) The delivering of Achior to the Jews

6.0.0.en: Prophesied: the words of Achior that appear as a prophecy are with God's help, to declare the truth before Holofernes, that perhaps he might fear God, otherwise divine punishment would come upon him. For God gives an opportunity for repentance to all people, even the wicked. After the men of Holofernes were angered by the words of Achior, thinking that he was an agent of the children of Israel and a deceiver of the Assyrians, the great anger of Holofernes then appeared, and he spoke with Achior the commander of the armies of the children of Ammon. He spoke in all pride, declaring the facts that would happen as he saw them: that the army of the Assyrians would strike the children of Israel as if they were striking one man, and by this their weakness and the weakness of their God would appear, like the rest of the gods of the nations, and it would then appear that the only god in the world is Nabuchodonosor; and then the Assyrians would kill Achior with them, and he would have only a little life left, so that he might see with his own eyes the death of the children of Israel with him. Holofernes, the commander of the Assyrian armies, continued his speech to Achior with all confidence, saying to him: Why are you in alarm and fear of this fate? For if your prophecy and your faith in what you said about the power of the God of Israel are true, no harm will come to you. The remarkable thing here is that Achior the Gentile did not have his faith shaken, but remained more confident in the power of the God of heaven than in the power of the armies of the Assyrians.

6.1.0.en: The sword of my army shall pierce your sides: one of the means of torture is that a person dies with the sword piercing his sides, that is, he dies a slow death, and is tormented, instead of having his head cut off, so that he dies and finds rest quickly. This method was used by the pagans and taken from them by the Jews (2 Sam 2:16), and it is a means that warriors use to frighten their enemies and to encourage themselves to destroy them.

6.1.1.en: Until: that is, after a very short period of time, counted in minutes.

6.1.2.en: Holofernes declared in anger to Achior that when he dies and is tormented with the sword piercing his forehead, he will be certain, by experiencing this torment, that there is no god in all the earth except Nabuchodonosor, by whose army's sword Achior will die. All this Achior will know as he breathes his last, with the Jews lying dead around him.

6.2.0.en: Holofernes continued his speech in pride, trying to plant fear in the heart of Achior, and said to him, why are you in alarm, so that your face has turned pale? Yet this did not happen, and Achior remained in his faith in the help of God, but the pride of Holofernes blinded his eyes, and made him imagine that Achior was in great fear.

6.2.1.en: So the devil always speaks with all confidence, as if he were reciting facts and conclusions that must be, to make us doubt the power of our God that protects us, and to make us fall into distress, alarm and despair, so that we forget that he is the liar and the father of lies. Hold fast, my brother, to your faith, however great the apparent power of the world may seem, for all the gods of the world and its powers are nothing before the power of your God. Declare your faith, confident that all the threats of the world are vain, and even if you are alone like Achior among the wicked who threaten you, you are stronger than they by the power of your God. If the faith of Achior the Gentile was like this, how much more should your faith be!

6.3.0.en: Then Holofernes issued his decree to seize Achior and deliver him to the people of Israel, so that he would die with them when the Assyrians attacked them.

6.4.0.en: Bethulia: a small city located north of the region of Samaria and northwest of the plain of Esdraelon.

6.4.1.en: It is thus on the northern front facing the invaders, who wanted to take possession of the land of the Jews in the region of Samaria, then the region of Judea, in which Jerusalem lies and in which is the temple of God. So the men of Holofernes seized Achior and went with him toward the city of Bethulia, in which the children of Israel dwell, which is built on a mountain.

6.5.1.en: Slings: plural of the sling, a simple weapon of war.

6.5.2.en: When the servants of Holofernes drew near the mountain on which the city of Bethulia stands, the men of war defending the city came out throwing stones with slings, for they thought that the servants of Holofernes were the vanguard of his army trying to attack the city.

6.6.0.en: Under the vengeance: when vengeance comes upon them.

6.6.1.en: So the Assyrians hurried to the side of the mountain to get out of range of the stones, lest they hit them, and they found a tree, and tied Achior to it and left him bound, and went back to Holofernes.

6.6.2.en: The devil, whom Holofernes signifies, in the extremity of his evil and his causing doubt in believers, leaves them to be bound to the Church – the place where believers gather – which Bethulia signifies, relying on his having bound them with the ropes of sin to the tree of material lusts; as he made Adam and Eve fall long ago by binding them with the desire to eat from the forbidden tree. Thus they are in the holy place but bound with evil lusts.

6.6.3.en: So be watchful, my brother, to the tricks of the devil, for he does not rejoice at your being in the Church among the believers and your being joined to the Holy Sacraments, but he wants to bind you with evil lusts so that you fall into sin in the holy place, and the fall is then greater.

6.6.4.en: Lift your eyes toward God, and He will loose you from the bonds of lust and give you, with the rest of the believers, the joy of fellowship with Him and His love. Be careful and attentive to the enticements of the devil at all times, even in the holy place.

6.7.s.en: (2) Achior tells the Jews what happened with Holofernes

6.7.0.en: When the soldiers of Bethulia were certain that the servants of Holofernes did not want to attack the city, but had done a strange act, namely binding a man to a tree at the bottom of the mountain, they came down and loosed Achior from his bonds and brought him up into the midst of the city, and he stood before the elders of the city and its people gathered with them; and they asked him why the Assyrians had bound him.

6.8.0.en: Ozias the son of Micah: Ozias (Uzziah) is a Hebrew word meaning the strength of God, and Micah is a Hebrew word meaning "who is like God," so that the whole of his name is the strength of God which has no like in the world. Ozias was not only one of the elders but their head, that is, the foremost head of the city and its leader, as appeared in (v. 19) when he held a feast for Achior, and also when the people protested against him and he asked them for a delay before surrendering the city (ch. 7). The tribe of Simeon: Simeon the son of Jacob, who angered God and his father when he killed, with his brother Levi, the men of the tribe of Hamor and Shechem (Gen 34). Judith also belongs to this tribe (ch. 8:1). Chabris (Karmi) the son of Gothoniel: Karmi is a Hebrew word meaning the worker in the vineyard, and Gothoniel is a Hebrew word meaning the strength of God, so the meaning of his name is "the strength of God working in the vineyard," and he is a type of Christ, who offered not only the juice of the grape but His blood on the cross.

6.8.1.en: Two rulers: that is, two foremost heads among the people, who were of the elders of the city who led it. The people chose them from among the wise and those who knew the Law, and they were usually of advanced age, to lead the people in the city as helpers to the high priest who was in Jerusalem, as we first heard of elders in the days of Moses, when his father-in-law Jethro advised him to do this to help him in judging the people (Ex 18). Achior explained to the people, and especially to the two elders, or foremost rulers, Ozias and Chabris, how he had informed Holofernes of the power of the God of Israel, the God of heaven, so that he became angry and sent him to die with the children of Israel. Two of the heads of the city, or its elders, are mentioned here: Ozias, the foremost head of the city, then Chabris, who is one of the well-known elders in it and who attended with the rest of the elders to learn the story of this man bound to a tree beside their city. These two heads are a type of Christ, the power of God and the Savior by His blood of His people.

6.8.2.en: And we see here that Ozias the head was of the tribe of Simeon, a tribe with which Jacob was angry because of its rashness in killing the tribe of Shechem, but God is able to bring strength out of weakness and to work in all His children.

6.9.0.en: Achior began to explain to the elders and people of Bethulia that he was the commander of the armies of the Ammonites and that he had stood with the rest of the commanders of the armies of the surrounding lands before Holofernes, who was angry because of their readiness to fight him; and how he had made clear to him the power of the God of the Jews, who cannot be resisted as long as the people are subject to Him and keep His commandments; then how the servants of Holofernes tried to kill him because he spoke of a God stronger than Nabuchodonosor.

6.10.1.en: Achior continued his speech, explaining how Holofernes commanded that he be bound and delivered to the Jews, so that he would take vengeance not only on him but on all the Jews, and Achior with them, when he attacks them and takes possession of their lands, and inflicts severe torments on Achior before he kills him.

6.10.2.en: The Jews who loosed Achior from his bonds signify the servants of the Church, who help a person to repent and be rid of the bonds of sin, and then bring him up to the Church, which the city of Bethulia, built on a mountain, signifies; for the Church is the image of heaven on earth, and the people signify the believers, the elders signify the priests, and Achior signifies the Gentiles, or those who are far off, who find their salvation in Christ within the Church when they believe in Him, so the power of God rescues them from Holofernes, who signifies Satan, and protects them within the Church.

6.10.3.en: I wish that we would rise above our worldly thoughts and the doubts of the devil and take refuge in the Church, so that all the thoughts of the enemy fall away from us, and we are strengthened by our being in the presence of Christ, among His priests and all the believers. Then our hearts take courage in the presence of the Church and its comforting, strengthening prayers.

6.11.s.en: (3) The prayer and the comforting of Achior

6.11.0.en: Their pride: their might and haughtiness.

6.11.2.en: Your saints: the fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob and all the men of God, the fathers of the people.

6.11.3.en: When the people heard the news of Holofernes and his power, and his insistence on taking vengeance on them, they took refuge quickly in God, prostrating themselves with reverence and humility before Him, and wept much, offering fervent prayers and supplications to God, declaring their weakness in great humility. They set out their problem, which was the strength of the enemies, who were fierce and very strong. But they asked God for His promises to their holy fathers, that is, they interceded by them and reminded Him of His tenderness toward the weak, for He is the strong One who helps His children in their afflictions, declaring their faith in the power of God more than in the power of the enemies, and also reminding God that He supports the weak who are humble and rejects the proud who rely on their own strength, that is, the enemies.

6.12.0.en: After all the people had finished their prayers, they rose reassured and joyful, for this is the natural result of true prayer offered to God. So they reassured Achior and comforted his heart that God would protect them and rescue them from the hands of Holofernes and his men.

6.12.1.en: However much the afflictions increase upon you, do not let your heart be troubled, but humble yourself and make supplication to God, confident that the power of God is displayed in the weakness of His children. Persevere in prayer even if many days pass in affliction, as the people of Bethulia persevered all day in prostration, weeping and prayer, for in the end God will comfort your heart and reassure you, and finally bring you out of all your afflictions. Seek the intercession of your beloved saints and do not be ashamed to remind God of His promises and mercies to His children, for He rejoices greatly in the prayer of His humble children; indeed, your humble prayer binds the power of Satan and keeps his harm from you.

6.13.0.en: Bestows this favor upon you: gives you this gift.

6.13.1.en: And the people said to Achior – perhaps this was spoken by the elders of the people such as Ozias and Chabris – that if Achior had believed in the God of Israel and had prophesied of His power, then let him be confident that he would see the salvation of God and the destruction of Holofernes and all his armies.

6.14.0.en: The people welcomed Achior and his household – if he should later wish to bring them – to dwell among them in Bethulia, as a Jew believing in the God of Israel, so that he would enjoy all his life the care of their God.

6.14.1.en: Stand firm in your faith in the midst of afflictions, and be confident that you will see the salvation of the Lord. Keep your place in the midst of the Church, that you may continue to enjoy God's care for you and your household all your life.

6.15.0.en: After the people gathered before God in prayer, they consulted the Lord, that is, they presented their problem to Him, believing in His ability to deliver them from it.

6.15.1.en: How beautiful it is that our counsel should be from God, and from His Church gathered for prayer in the form and on the tongue of her spiritual fathers. It is better than any human counsel, for the counsel of God is what protects a person and truly supports him.

6.16.0.en: The people departed, each to his house, to eat food after fasting all day, and all rejoiced in the comfort of God. And Ozias the head of the city called all the people again to gather and to continue praying all night, that God might intervene and rescue His people, which confirms that this was a spiritual supper, and that they were not slack in their striving to give their bodies rest.

6.16.1.en: If God comforts your heart and reassures you, it is so that you may continue your striving. Night, in the view of the people of the world, is an opportunity for laxity and idleness, even for amusement and play, but for the children of God it is an opportunity for spiritual vigil, and therefore the Church ordained the Midnight Prayer, that the night might be blessed with prayer, and ordained also the Midnight Praise (Tasbeha), that our hearts might be lifted up in praise and thanksgiving to God. Thus Satan the enemy finds us in constant spiritual wakefulness, and cannot overcome us. Night also signifies the darkness and evil of the people of the world, so we need to be watchful all the days of our life in continual prayers.
